title: Distordia Agent Card Standard (v0.2.0 draft)
description: Consolidated successor to agent.v0.1.0 AND the swarm registration half of swarm.v0.1.0. Premise: a Distordia agent HAS ITS OWN SIGCHAIN, so identity, ownership, signing and transacting are native Nexus capabilities and must not be re-declared here. What Nexus does NOT provide is DISCOVERY (finding an agent by what it does), ENDPOINT BINDING (proving an off-chain endpoint belongs to an on-chain identity), and TRUST (a revocable vouching credential). This card provides exactly those three things and nothing else. A swarm is the same card with kind='swarm' and membership expressed as a token holding. See docs/agent-swarm-nexus-alignment-note.md.
supersedesStandard: agent.v0.1.0.json and the SwarmRegistration definition of swarm.v0.1.0.json (both retained for history)
maxSize: 1KB (system fields ~180 bytes, ~820 bytes for data). Detailed capability data (structured skills, IO modes, rate limits, model, pricing) lives in the OFF-CHAIN extended card referenced by card-uri and integrity-checked by card-hash -- the same body-off-chain/anchor-on-chain pattern as content.v0.2.0.

premise.ownSigchain: The agent authenticates with its own Nexus signature chain. Its genesis is the auto-assigned 'owner' of this asset, so agent identity needs no field here.
premise.nativeNotRedeclared: Nexus natively provides: identity (genesis), human-readable naming (namespace::name), signing keys (crypto object register), token/NXS accounts, and settlement (conditional contracts / invoices). None of these are duplicated as fields.
premise.sovereigntyConsequence: A sovereign sigchain CANNOT be shut down by a third party. There is therefore no 'kill-switch' flag (v0.1.0's was unenforceable: only the asset owner could write it). The enforceable mechanism is the REVOCABLE OPERATING CREDENTIAL in 'credential' -- an authority stops vouching, and counterparties refuse to deal. Revocation is enforceable; a self-owned boolean is not.
premise.spendingLimits: v0.1.0's can-transact / can-sign / max-tx-value are dropped. An agent with its own sigchain can transact by definition, and Nexus cannot today enforce delegated spending caps (the Sigchain Ledger VM is roadmap). A real cap is achieved by FUNDING a dedicated account to the intended ceiling.

self-addr.description: Queryable copy of this asset's own register address (the auto-assigned 'address' is not filterable in register/list). Stamped post-create.

status.description: Card lifecycle state. Note this is the AGENT'S OWN declaration; independent trust comes from 'credential'.

kind.description: Whether this card describes a single agent or a swarm (a collective). A swarm uses the same card and expresses membership via 'members-token'.

agent.description: Human-readable native Nexus name of this agent, normally a name inside the operator's namespace, e.g. 'acme.corp::logistics.agent01'. The cryptographic identity is the asset's own 'owner' genesis; this field is for resolution and display.

operator.description: NAMESPACE of the organization that operates and vouches for this agent. Nexus namespace rules apply: lowercase letters, numbers and periods only (hyphens are INVALID on-chain).

caps.description: Comma-separated capability tags for DISCOVERY (e.g. 'route-optimization,dispatch,tracking'). Coarse by design -- structured skills with IO modes live in the off-chain card. This is the primary thing Nexus cannot provide: finding an agent by what it does.

endpoint-a2a.description: Agent-to-Agent protocol endpoint. Binding is proven by signing responses with the key in 'key-slot'/'pubkey' -- an unsigned endpoint claim is not evidence of control.

endpoint-mcp.description: Model Context Protocol endpoint. Same signature-binding rule as endpoint-a2a.

key-slot.description: Which slot of the agent sigchain's native CRYPTO OBJECT REGISTER is used to sign endpoint responses and A2A messages.

pubkey.description: Public key (or its hash) corresponding to 'key-slot', published so counterparties can verify signed messages and endpoint control without a prior relationship.

credential.description: self-addr of a REVOCABLE operating credential/attestation issued by an authority (typically the operator or a Distordia attester). This is the enforceable safety mechanism replacing v0.1.0's kill-switch: a sovereign sigchain cannot be shut down, but vouching can be withdrawn. Consumers MUST check the credential is still valid, not merely that this card says 'active'.

members-token.description: For kind='swarm': address of the token register whose holders ARE the members. Membership becomes countable, provable, and revocable on-chain -- replacing v0.1.0's 256-char pipe-separated 'members' string (which capped swarm size and proved nothing). Empty for kind='agent'.

card-uri.description: Location of the extended off-chain agent card (ar:// / ipfs:// / https), holding structured skills, IO modes, rate limits, model details and pricing. Rate limits are advisory and enforced by the serving endpoint, never by the chain.

card-hash.description: SHA-256 of the extended card for integrity ('sha256:...').

supersedes.description: self-addr of the prior card revision this replaces (append-only revision).

droppedFromV010._comment: Fields deliberately removed because a sigchain-owning agent makes them redundant or unenforceable.
droppedFromV010.agent-id + namespace: Replaced by the native namespace::name in 'agent' plus the owner genesis.
droppedFromV010.can-transact / can-sign: An agent with its own sigchain can transact and sign by definition.
droppedFromV010.max-tx-value: Not chain-enforceable as an integer. Fund a dedicated account to the intended ceiling instead.
droppedFromV010.kill-switch / kill-auth: Unenforceable: only the asset owner can write its own asset. Replaced by the revocable 'credential'.
droppedFromV010.rate-rpm / rate-rpd: Inherently off-chain and advisory; moved to the extended card.
droppedFromV010.model / context-window: Moved to the extended off-chain card.
droppedFromV010.swarm-id / swarm-role / member-count / m: Swarm registration is absorbed here via kind='swarm' + members-token. Counters and reputation must be DERIVED by querying agreement assets, not self-asserted.

examples._comment: An autonomous agent with its own sigchain, operated by acme.corp.
A swarm: same card, kind='swarm', membership = holders of the swarm token.

queryFilters.discoverByCapability: distordia-type = 'agent-card' AND status = 'active' AND caps LIKE '%route-optimization%'

nexus.verifyAgent: 1) resolve the card; 2) confirm the 'credential' asset is still valid (not revoked/expired); 3) challenge the endpoint and verify the signature against 'pubkey'. Do NOT trust 'status' alone -- it is self-declared.

notes: This standard exists because Nexus provides identity, ownership and settlement but NOT discovery, endpoint binding, or trust. Everything a sigchain already gives an agent has been removed.
Agent sovereignty is the key safety insight: an agent with its own sigchain cannot be switched off by anyone, so safety must be built on revocable vouching (credential), not on a self-owned flag.
Swarm registration is absorbed here (kind='swarm'); swarm MISSIONS move to the generic agreement standard (agreement.v0.2.0.json).
Track record and reputation are DERIVED by querying distordia-agreement assets where this agent is a party -- never stored as self-written counters.
Successor to agent.v0.1.0 (standards/agent-standard.json) and the SwarmRegistration half of swarm.v0.1.0 (standards/swarm-standard.json); both retained for history.
